headline: Philippine Peso Ends Four-Day Drop on Profit-Taking and Lower Oil
summary: The Philippine peso snapped a four-day losing streak against the US dollar, supported by trader profit-taking and lower global crude oil prices.
why: The Philippines is a net energy importer, making the peso particularly sensitive to international crude oil price movements.

impacts.name: Philippine Peso
impacts.why: Lower global crude prices reduced import bill expectations, boosting domestic currency value.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Trader profit-taking after a four-day decline combined with lower international oil import costs boosted the Philippine peso.
